statusNote: Since 2019 the institution has run a two-tier top-leadership structure: John MacArthur held the newly created title of Chancellor (2019-2025, until his death) as senior spiritual/institutional authority, while a separate President served as chief executive. 'President' is used here as the operating top-leader title; MacArthur's Chancellor role is captured as a note on his entry.

leaders.priorInstitution: Grace Community Church, Sun Valley, CA (continued concurrently)
leaders.nextRole: Chancellor, The Master's University and Seminary
leaders.notes: Longtime pastor of Grace Community Church who became president in 1985 (institution renamed The Master's College). Stepped down as president in June 2019 to become Chancellor, a new senior title he held until his death on July 14, 2025 at age 86.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President / VP for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Longtime faculty member (since 1970) and administrator who stepped in as interim president when MacArthur moved to the chancellor role; returned to a senior VP role after Sam Horn's appointment.

leaders.priorInstitution: Central Baptist Theological Seminary, Plymouth, MN (and prior EVP roles at Bob Jones University)
leaders.notes: Unanimously elected TMU's 9th president in Feb 2020; resigned February 26, 2021 after just over a year in the role, capping a period of internal tumult at the institution. Board gave no specific reason.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor of Biblical Studies / Endowed Research Chair
leaders.notes: Longtime TMU faculty member (since 2004) named interim president in March 2021 after Horn's resignation; board affirmed him as full-time (permanent) president effective May 6, 2022. Currently serving.

20-year presidency (record length for the institution); led the transition from Findlay College to University of Findlay and tripled enrollment and endowment in his first decade. Prior career and post-retirement activity not well documented in available sources.

leaders.priorInstitution: Ohio Northern University (also previously president of Monmouth College, IL, and dean at Mount Union College, OH)
leaders.notes: Career college president (also led Ohio Northern University for 20 years and Monmouth College for 5) and Army veteran; stabilized Findlay financially and grew faculty and doctoral programs. Died in 2020 at age 94.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Advancement / Chief Development Officer
leaders.priorInstitution: Centenary College of Louisiana, Shreveport, LA
leaders.notes: First female president in Findlay's history; joined in 2010 after 24 years at Centenary College (professor of English, then VP for advancement). Announced retirement in 2025, stepping down at the end of the 2025-2026 school year after 16 years.

leaders.priorInstitution: University of St. Thomas, Houston, TX
leaders.notes: Named University of Findlay's 18th president effective July 1, 2026, succeeding Katherine Fell. Previously grew enrollment and fundraising as president of University of St. Thomas (Houston); also held roles as president of Independent Colleges of Indiana and provost at St. Gregory's University. Currently serving.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost
leaders.nextRole: Returned to UTC in 2004-2005 as interim chancellor; otherwise retired
leaders.notes: 16-year tenure (1981-1997) that expanded academic programs significantly; later came back as interim chancellor 2004-2005. Died July 24, 2026 at age 91.

leaders.priorInstitution: California State University San Marcos (previously president of Southeast Missouri State University)
leaders.notes: Resigned as chancellor in 2004 amid tensions with the UT System; went on to serve as headmaster of Baylor School. Died in January 2024 at age 85.
Brought back as interim chancellor for one year to bridge the gap after Stacy's departure, before Roger Brown's arrival.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: University of North Carolina at Pembroke
leaders.notes: Announced early retirement effective September 30, 2012. No formal post-retirement academic role documented in available sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor of Leadership and Policy Studies (retired)
leaders.notes: Veteran higher-ed administrator (former chancellor of LSU Shreveport and interim chancellor of LSU Baton Rouge) who came out of retirement to serve as UTC's interim chancellor from September 2012 until Steven Angle's arrival in July 2013.
Led UTC for over 11 years (July 2013-2024/2025); stepped down and transitioned to a faculty role in UTC's Chemistry department rather than leaving the institution.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Gary W. Rollins College of Business
leaders.notes: UTC alumnus (BA 1983) named interim chancellor effective Jan 1, 2025, serving as a bridge until Lori Mann Bruce's arrival; publicly ruled himself out for the permanent role.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Approved by the UT Board of Trustees as UTC's chancellor effective June 30, 2025. Currently serving.

statusNote: This is Touro's flagship New York institution, founded as Touro College in 1970-71 and renamed Touro University in 2022. It also serves as the headquarters campus for the broader multi-school 'Touro University' system (formerly 'Touro College and University System'), which is distinct from the separately accredited Touro University California and Touro University Nevada. Only two people have led it as president since founding.

leaders.priorTitle: Sociology Professor / Dean, Bernard Revel Graduate School
leaders.notes: Founding president; an ordained rabbi with a Columbia PhD in sociology, he founded Touro College in 1970-71 and led it until his death on February 8, 2010 at age 94.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Provost and Chief Operating Officer
leaders.priorInstitution: Touro College (previously Distinguished Professor of Cardiology / Associate Chief of Cardiology, Northwestern University)
leaders.notes: A cardiologist by training (Northwestern Memorial's Bluhm Cardiovascular Institute), he joined Touro in 2009 as COO with the board signaling he would succeed Lander; became president in 2010 and oversaw major growth including the 2012 acquisition of New York Medical College and the 2022 Touro College-to-Touro University name change. Currently serving.
